text.p: Venezuela's inflation rate in September was 3.6 percent, up from 3.3 percent in September 1995 but down from 4.1 percent in August, the Central Bank said.
September's inflation rate brings inflation over the past 12 months to 115.2 percent, compared to 51.8 percent in the year to September 1995, the bank said.

It was the fourth successive drop in the monthly rate since a peak of 12.6 percent in May. The government launched an economic reform program in April which set free currency and interest rates and increased gasoline prices fivefold.
Accumulated inflation for the nine months of the year now stands at 83.7 percent, compared to 33.7 percent at the same stage in 1995.

Government officials have predicted that inflation rates will drop steadily to reach no more than two percent per month at the end of the year. Inflation for 1996 will end at 95 percent, compared to 56.6 percent in 1995, they have said.

The central bank said the fall in the monthly inflation rate in September "indicate that inflationary expectations have fallen as was expected within the context of the economic stabilization program initiated in April."

"Clothing and shoes" was the category which registered the highest price rise in September, rising 4.8 percent. "Various expenditures" and "food, drinks and tobacco" followed with rises of 3.6 percent and "household expenditures" rose 3.2 percent.
